clue.text: Certain care is lousy for jail

indicators.note: lousy means poor or botched, so the letters of the two words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that careless treatment of a prisoner justifies locking them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousy' rearranges CERTAIN CARE, all eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To jail someone is to imprison or confine them; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Row with denials embracing single sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the word for denials wraps around the single letter

parts.note: noes or nos are refusals, denials
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A quarrel in which a lover's refusals wrap around one darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as the heart of 'sweet', its central E.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a loud din or racket, and so is a noise.

clue.text: Slow movement from author after article

indicators.note: after places the author's name behind the article in the answer

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Dante, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A sluggish musical passage composed by a writer, following some piece in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' is a section of a symphony, not physical motion.
explanation.definitionFit: An andante is a musical piece or section played at a moderately slow, walking tempo.

indicators.note: catching means trapping inside, so the scream holds the tool

parts.note: to cry is to scream
an awl is a pointed tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: Something spooky makes someone shriek, while something else is merely dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring thing' is a tool that bores holes, not something tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy-crawly things make the skin creep; crawly is an informal word for creepy or skin-crawling.

indicators.note: in a down entry elevated means lifted upwards, so the word for by reads bottom to top

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
lying is dishonesty

explanation.surface: Answering back by means of grand, lofty deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns PER upward to give REP.
explanation.definitionFit: To riposte is to make a quick retort, so riposting is answering back.

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken in within, so the answer sits inside the two words

explanation.surface: A government department winds up being swallowed by its own minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'Minister, Ministry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end points, such as the final stations of rail lines.

clue.text: Hearing Independent State contains endless scrap

indicators.note: contains means holds within, so the independent-plus-state pair wraps the shortened scrap

parts.note: a nation is a state

indicators.note: endless means without its final letter, so the last letter of the scrap is dropped

parts.note: a vestige is a trace or scrap of something

explanation.surface: A political report on an independent country riddled with fragments of an old quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but means a leftover trace; 'Hearing' is a judicial inquiry, not the sense of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing, as in a judicial inquiry, is a formal investigation into a matter.

parts.note: collared suggests an arrested criminal, but it is a clergyman in a dog collar, whose house goes with the parish

explanation.surface: Where might someone just arrested be lodged?
explanation.walkthrough: 'collared' wants to mean arrested, pointing at a cell; the collar is the clerical dog collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Church of England parish priest lives in the house provided by the church for him or her.

indicators.note: tipsily means in a drunken, unsteady way, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A merry guest admits being amused while getting fuzzy-headed from drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsily' rearranges I'M ENTERTAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazy is vague and unclear, not precisely fixed.

clue.text: New commercial includes excellent, fantastic girl

indicators.note: includes means holds inside, so the new commercial takes in the letters for excellent

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
A1 means first-rate, excellent

explanation.surface: A fresh advert features a wonderful young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' means belonging to fantasy or myth, not marvellous. AI stands for A1, first class.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek mythology, a fabled maiden.

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for being goes round the single letter

parts.note: a person is a being
I, the first person, an individual

explanation.surface: Defamation occurs when someone circles around a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging, disparaging remark, a slur on someone's name.

clue.text: Always consort with English flier first

indicators.note: first places the English flier ahead of the consort

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, a flier
to consort with is to ally oneself

explanation.surface: An instruction always to keep company with an English pilot before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests an airman but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means for ever, at all times, which is what always means.

clue.text: Initially indignant, rather angry, then enraged

definitions.text: Initially indignant, rather angry, then enraged

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A mood that escalates from indignation through anger to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer from its initials and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indignant, angry and enraged is furious, cross and incensed.

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for without reads in reverse

parts.note: less means without, as in 'less tax'

explanation.surface: Soldiers lacking support are given a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but is the turnaround signal; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is an ornamental tuft of threads hung from cushions, curtains or caps.

clue.text: Very poor leader of Senate cornered

indicators.note: leader of means the front letter of the following word

parts.note: trapped means cornered

explanation.surface: A dreadful head of the upper chamber is backed into a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very poor' looks like a verdict on the leader but means short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped, as in strapped for cash, is informal for hard up, lacking funds.

definitions.meaning: verb: to declare or hint, as in intimating an intention

explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to state or make known, and intimate matters are private, personal ones.

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's note to verify an alteration to medication levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges IN plus DOSAGE; 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose a disease is to identify and establish it from symptoms, settling what it is.

indicators.note: somehow means by some unspecified means, so the letters fall into another order

explanation.surface: A gardener's view that a shrub needs some kind of drainage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed for' is a link; the anagram signal is the adverb before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardenia is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Maiden Queen's captured by period author

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the period wraps the maiden and queen's letters

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
ER, Elizabeth Regina, with 's, gives ERS

explanation.surface: A historical novel in which a young woman and the queen's household are taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period author' looks like a writer of historical fiction; 'period' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist and poet.

indicators.note: follows puts the word for judge behind the word for concerned with

parts.note: re means concerning, about
to deem is to judge or consider

explanation.surface: A magistrate takes a case relating to someone's release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb, consider, not a court official.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a debt or pledge is to pay it off, settling or discharging the obligation.

clue.text: Back runner losing head after tip

indicators.note: after puts the beheaded runner behind the tip

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

indicators.note: losing head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A betting picture: backing a runner that falls behind after a tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' and 'tip' both look like racing bets; 'losing head' cuts HORSE to ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to support it publicly, to back it.

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so male plus one's swallows the second insect

parts.note: one's read as one is, I'S, Roman one plus is
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A male insect that devours another insect, as the female praying mantis notoriously eats her mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', the Roman numeral plus IS; 'Insect' appears twice, once as definition and once as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The mantis, or praying mantis, is a predatory insect with folded forelegs.

indicators.note: are pronounced means the two letters are spoken as their names

parts.note: the ends of the word top are its outer letters, T and P, which said as letter names sound like the tent

explanation.surface: A camper remarks that the peaks of a shelter stand out clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like prominent; it means the letters T and P are said out loud as 'tee pee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent of skins or canvas used by Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: Soldier in drama with guns shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A trooper in a play featuring gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges DRAMA plus GUNS; it looks like gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardsman is a member of a regiment of guards, a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Reminders being married, a little upset

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the word for a little reads bottom to top

parts.note: some means a little, as in 'have some'

explanation.surface: Notes that come with being married leave one slightly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like distressed; it turns SOME upwards to EMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Memos are brief written notes to jog the memory or pass on instructions.

clue.text: Drive off in Open, go too far?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the word for drive off sits inside the word for open

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
to shoo is to drive away an animal

explanation.surface: A golfer hits the ball off the tee at the Open and sends it too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'Open' suggest golf, but 'Drive off' means to chase away and 'Open' means not hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot a target or runway is to pass beyond it, going further than intended.

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the session and Republican letters read backwards

parts.note: a time is a session or spell, as in 'a good time'

explanation.surface: A short meeting in which a Republican is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective, short; it is a noun, a set of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the area of responsibility assigned to someone, their terms of reference.

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the two words carry the answer within them

explanation.surface: An athlete's perseverance keeps them in a place on the team now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from inside 'Sprinter's' into 'persevering'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersperse things is to scatter them here and there among others.
